faq.q1: Where can I find pet-friendly restaurants in Hong Kong?
faq.a1: You can find them across Hong Kong Island, Kowloon, and the New Territories, and filter by district to find nearby options.
faq.q2: What should I check before bringing my dog to a restaurant?
faq.a2: Check whether pets are allowed indoors, whether reservations are required, and if walk-ins are accepted before visiting.
faq.q3: How can I tell if a restaurant is truly pet-friendly?
faq.a3: Look for verification badges, policy tags, ratings, and real user feedback on pet access and dining experience.
faq.q4: Can I walk in, or do I need a reservation?
faq.a4: It depends on the venue policy. Use the walk-in filter or check each restaurant's entry policy label.
faq.q5: What's the difference between the FEHD list and PetWell verified restaurants?
faq.a5: The FEHD list shows licence-approved premises allowing dogs. PetWell verification means our team called to confirm pet policies including indoor access and walk-in rules.
faq.q6: What rules apply at FEHD-approved restaurants?
faq.a6: Typical rules include leashing, no dogs on tables, no contact with utensils, and no access to kitchen areas. See FEHD for full details.
faq.q7: Can I bring my cat to pet-friendly restaurants?
faq.a7: Policies vary. PetWell listings focus on dog-friendly venues — call ahead to confirm if cats are welcome.
faq.q8: Which areas have the most pet-friendly restaurants?
faq.a8: Hong Kong Island (Central, Wan Chai, Eastern) and Kowloon (Yau Tsim Mong, Kwun Tong) tend to have more options. Browse our 18-district pages for counts.

methodology.title: How the CANINE PRO allergy report is interpreted
methodology.desc1: The CANINE PRO allergy report detects specific IgE antibodies from serum using a quantitative enzyme immunoblot assay. Reaction intensity is scanned optically and converted into allergen-specific IgE titers.
methodology.desc2: Results are expressed in AU/mL and attributed to RAST class 0 to 3: not found, moderate, serious, and severe. The report covers mites and mould, plants and pollens, food allergens, insects, and miscellaneous allergens.

faq.q1: What does the allergy test measure?
faq.a1: It measures allergen-specific IgE antibody levels from serum and reports them as AU/mL with RAST class 0 to 3.
faq.q2: Which pets may benefit from testing?
faq.a2: Pets with suspected allergy, recurring skin irritation, respiratory signs, gastrointestinal signs, or unexplained sensitivity may be candidates after veterinary assessment.
faq.q3: Is PCR the same as an allergy test?
faq.a3: No. PCR screening looks for pathogen genetic material, while IgE allergy testing evaluates immune response to allergens.

petMatchmaker.intro: Finding the right pet isn't just about what's cute—it's about matching their lifestyle to yours. From the chirpy energy of a bird to the quiet hops of a rabbit, let's find out who your soul-pet actually is. Answer these 5 questions!
petMatchmaker.question: Question

dog.title: You should get a Dog!
dog.description: You have an active lifestyle and plenty of love to give. You want a partner in crime who will go outside with you, greet you enthusiastically, and participate in your daily routine. You don't mind a little noise or mud.

cat.title: You should get a Cat!
cat.description: You want a companion who is affectionate but independent. You appreciate a pet that fits into your current routine without needing constant supervision. You like quiet evenings and warm snuggles on the sofa.

bird.title: You should get a Bird!
bird.description: You are smart, social, and maybe a little quirky! You don't mind noise (in fact, you might like the singing or talking) and you want a pet that is highly intelligent and interactive. You are okay with cleaning up seeds and feathers.

rabbit.title: You should get a Rabbit!
rabbit.description: You want something softer and quieter than a dog, but more interactive than a hamster. You have space for them to hop around safely and you don't mind pet-proofing your cords. You love the idea of a gentle, social vegetarian friend.

reptile.title: You should get a Reptile or Fish!
reptile.description: You prefer a low-pressure pet that is fascinating to observe. You might have allergies, or you simply prefer a quiet home. You enjoy curating a habitat (tank or terrarium) and appreciate the aesthetic of a pet that doesn't demand constant physical affection.

q1.question: Let's talk about noise. What is your tolerance level?
q1.a: I don't mind barking or active noise; a quiet house feels empty!
q1.b: I like it mostly quiet, just some occasional meows or purring.
q1.c: I love chatter, whistling, or even some loud squawking—it's festive!
q1.d: I prefer almost total silence, maybe just some gentle chewing sounds.
q1.e: I want zero noise from my pet.

q2.question: How much space can you dedicate to a pet?
q2.a: I have a yard or access to parks and plenty of floor space.
q2.b: My apartment/house is their kingdom; they can roam everywhere.
q2.c: I have space for a large vertical cage and room for them to fly safely.
q2.d: I have a designated "pen" area or a room where they can hop freely.
q2.e: I have a sturdy table or shelf for a tank/enclosure, but limited floor space.

q3.question: What kind of "mess" are you willing to deal with?
q3.a: Muddy paws, shed hair, and slobber.
q3.b: Dealing with a litter box and occasional scratched furniture.
q3.c: Seeds, hulls, and feathers scattered around a cage.
q3.d: Hay... lots of hay. And cleaning a litter tray daily.
q3.e: Cleaning algae or changing bedding/water once a week.

q4.question: How do you want to interact with your pet?
q4.b: Petting them while I watch TV, or playing with a laser pointer.
q4.c: Teaching them tricks, whistling tunes, or having them sit on my shoulder.
q4.d: Sitting on the floor with them and letting them nudge me for treats.
q4.e: Watching them explore their tank; looking but not touching.

q5.question: If you leave the house for 8 hours, what is your pet doing?
q5.a: Waiting by the door (or maybe needing a dog walker).
q5.b: Sleeping in a sunbeam, completely unbothered.
q5.c: Playing with toys in their cage, possibly listening to the radio I left on.
q5.d: Sleeping in their hutch or safe pen area with plenty of hay.
q5.e: Just swimming or basking under their heat lamp.
